translationRepairs: Huxia: the second character is pronounced with the bei initial and pan final.
s0150 虎𤳖下北潘切 is a fanqie note for the personal-name headword continued in s0151–s0152, not a place name; 'Bielian Dou' is invented, and the proposed Huxia pronunciation gloss matches the Chinese.
Huxia — the lower character uses the bei pan cut.
The literal likewise invents place-name Bielian Dou; 下北潘切 is a bei-pan cut on the lower character of 虎𤳖, and the proposed replacement renders that note correctly.
s0162 is 塔里捨 地名, a place-name gloss like the neighboring entries; 'Annals of Emperor Daozong' is a displaced header, and Talise restores the place name.
Literal 'Annals of Daozong' does not render 塔里捨 地名; the proposed Talise place-name gloss matches the Chinese.
Sacrifice to the East: by national custom all sacrifices face east, hence the name.
s0185 defines 祭東 as the east-facing sacrifice custom; 'Treatise on Rites' is a displaced title, and the proposed gloss matches 國俗，凡祭皆東向，故曰祭東.
Ji Dong — a state custom: all sacrifices face east, hence called Sacrifice to the East.
Literal 'Rites Treatise' is not a rendering of 祭東; the proposed Ji Dong state-custom gloss accurately follows the Chinese definition.
Sacrifice to the East: by national custom all sacrifices face east, hence the name.
Dilie Madu: an official in charge of ceremonial affairs.
s0186 is 敵烈麻都 掌禮官, a rites-official title; the current idiomatic still carries the prior 祭東 gloss, and Dilie Madu restores the correct headword.
s0233 抹里 官府名 names a government office; '<Note 6>' is a displaced marker, and the proposed Moli office-name gloss matches the Chinese.
Literal '<Six>' is not a translation of 抹里 官府名; the proposed Moli office-name gloss is accurate.
Jinzao: the second character uses the zu cong cut.
s0267 金㚇下祖叢切 is a fanqie pronunciation note, not a treatise title; the proposed Jinzao zu-cong cut gloss matches the Chinese.
Jinzao — the second character uses the zu cong cut.
Literal 'Rites and Guard Treatise' invents a section header; 下祖叢切 is the fanqie for the lower character of 金㚇, correctly restored by the proposal.
Shili Xuegun: the ceremonial crown worn for the Mount Muye sacrifice.
Shili Xuegun: the ceremonial crown worn for the mountain-worship rite.
s0272 has 行拜山禮則服之, the mountain-worship rite; Mount Muye is not in the Chinese, and the proposed wording removes that invention.
Cha: the first character is pronounced dan.
Dan: the first character is pronounced dan.
s0277 上音誕 marks the upper character's reading as dan; 'Cha' contradicts that fanqie, and 'Dan' restores the indicated pronunciation.
The literal likewise names the headword Cha against 音誕; replacing it with Dan matches the stated pronunciation.
Mofu He: a title for tribal chiefs; also rendered Mofu He.
Mofu He: a title for tribal chiefs; also called Mofu Ho.

s0301 distinguishes headword 莫弗紇 from the variant 莫弗賀; the original and the proposed after leave both forms as identical 'Mofu He' (the proposal also inserts Chinese into the English field), so the variant is rendered Mofu Ho.
